CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right leg pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
43-year-old patient presents with right upper leg pain sustained while bowling. Patient was running up to the lane with bowling ball held back when she swung it forward and struck her right leg instead of the lane, causing her to fall. Patient denies significant swelling but reports some bruising on the back aspect of the leg. Patient reports difficulty walking and describes pain as very sore with weight-bearing. Patient states she would avoid stairs at all costs, though she does not have stairs at home. Currently managing pain with alternating ibuprofen and acetaminophen.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Atopic eczema.
Diverticulosis with subsequent diverticulitis, treated with partial colectomy.

MEDICATIONS
Fluocinonide for eczema, used as needed when itching worsens.
Ibuprofen as needed for pain.
Acetaminophen as needed for pain.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Recreational bowling.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Significant tenderness to the lateral aspect of the right upper leg. No pain or tenderness with flexion or extension of the lower leg.

RESULTS
X-ray of femur: normal, no evidence of fracture or swelling.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Contusion of right upper leg. Initiated mobic 15 mg once daily for anti-inflammatory effect. Recommended ice for pain management. Expected resolution within one week. Patient instructed to return if symptoms do not improve.
